source: Whenly published questions from the Google Sheet (local backup sheet-backup-2026-10-06), dated 2026-07-26 to 2026-10-05

items.prompt: When was Doctor Who first broadcast on the BBC?
items.reveal: Answer: 1963. The day after JFK was shot, which rather stole its thunder.

items.prompt: When was the National Health Service founded?
items.reveal: Answer: 1948. Aneurin Bevan's big idea.

items.prompt: When did Tim Berners-Lee write the proposal that became the World Wide Web?
items.reveal: Answer: 1989. "Vague but exciting," wrote his boss on the cover.

items.prompt: When did the original Mini go on sale?
items.reveal: Answer: 1959. Designed by Alec Issigonis. Four wheels, next to no boot, and endless charm.

items.prompt: When did Live Aid fill Wembley Stadium for famine relief?
items.reveal: Answer: 1985. Queen stole the show in twenty minutes flat.

items.prompt: When did Coronation Street air its very first episode?
items.reveal: Answer: 1960. Still going strong.

items.prompt: When did Alexander Fleming spot the stray mould that gave us penicillin?
items.reveal: Answer: 1928. The tidiest accident in medical history began in a very untidy lab.

items.prompt: When did Big Ben, the bell, ring out for the first time?
items.reveal: Answer: 1859. The bell, not the tower. That one's worth points down the pub.

items.prompt: When did Queen release Bohemian Rhapsody as a single?
items.reveal: Answer: 1975. Six minutes long. The record company nearly fainted.

items.prompt: When did Sir Clive Sinclair's ZX Spectrum go on sale?
items.reveal: Answer: 1982. 48K of memory and a loading screech you can still hear now.

items.prompt: When did the Spice Girls release their debut single, Wannabe?
items.reveal: Answer: 1996. Girl power arrived.

items.prompt: When did Monty Python's Flying Circus first appear on the BBC?
items.reveal: Answer: 1969. And now for something completely different.

items.prompt: When was Louise Brown, the world's first IVF baby, born in Oldham?
items.reveal: Answer: 1978.

items.prompt: When did Blackpool Tower open to the public?
items.reveal: Answer: 1894. The Eiffel Tower, but with more rock and donkeys.

items.prompt: When did the United Kingdom join the European Economic Community?
items.reveal: Answer: 1973. In on New Year's Day. Leaving took rather longer.

items.prompt: When did Concorde make its maiden flight?
items.reveal: Answer: 1969. Mach 2, a droopy nose, and dinner in New York before you left.

items.prompt: When did Fawlty Towers first check in on BBC Two?
items.reveal: Answer: 1975. Twelve episodes. Not one of them wasted.

items.prompt: When did Cadbury launch its Dairy Milk bar?
items.reveal: Answer: 1905. A glass and a half of full-cream milk, and a nation hooked.

items.prompt: When did Rick Astley's Never Gonna Give You Up hit number one in the UK?
items.reveal: Answer: 1987. Decades early for its true calling: the internet's oldest prank.

items.prompt: When did The Great British Bake Off first air?
items.reveal: Answer: 2010. Cakes, a tent, and the gentlest reality TV ever made.

items.prompt: When was the Penny Black, the world's first adhesive postage stamp, issued?
items.reveal: Answer: 1840. Rowland Hill's idea. Lick, stick, and away it went.

items.prompt: When was the Angel of the North installed near Gateshead?
items.reveal: Answer: 1998. 175 tonnes of rusty steel, with wings wider than a jumbo jet.

items.prompt: When did Wham! release Last Christmas?
items.reveal: Answer: 1984. Kept off number one at the time. Utterly immortal since.

items.prompt: When did Decimal Day arrive, swapping shillings for new pence?
items.reveal: Answer: 1971. Farewell half-crowns, farthings and thruppenny bits.

items.prompt: When did The Beano publish its very first issue?
items.reveal: Answer: 1938.

items.prompt: When did the Eden Project open its giant biomes in a Cornish clay pit?
items.reveal: Answer: 2001. The world's biggest greenhouses, dropped into a hole near St Austell.

items.prompt: When did the world's first underground railway open, in London?
items.reveal: Answer: 1863. Steam trains. Underground. The Victorians feared absolutely nothing.

items.prompt: When did the first Raspberry Pi, a tiny British computer, go on sale?
items.reveal: Answer: 2012. A credit-card-sized computer for about 25 pounds. It sold out in hours.

items.prompt: When did Halley's Comet last swing past Earth?
items.reveal: Answer: 1986. Next due in 2061.

items.prompt: When did London introduce its congestion charge?
items.reveal: Answer: 2003. Ken Livingstone's fiver to drive into town.

items.prompt: When did the Sinclair C5 battery tricycle go on sale?
items.reveal: Answer: 1985. 15mph, and terrifying next to a lorry.

items.prompt: When was Marmite first produced, in Burton-on-Trent?
items.reveal: Answer: 1902. Yeast extract from brewers' leftovers. Divisive from day one.

items.prompt: When was Three Lions first released?
items.reveal: Answer: 1996. For the European Championship held in England.

items.prompt: When did England bring in the 5p charge for carrier bags?
items.reveal: Answer: 2015. And suddenly everyone owned nineteen bags for life.

items.prompt: When did The Italian Job, with its Mini getaway, open in cinemas?
items.reveal: Answer: 1969. Michael Caine, three Minis and a coach left hanging over a cliff.

items.prompt: When did the Sony Walkman go on sale?
items.reveal: Answer: 1979. Suddenly your music came with you.

items.prompt: When did Waddingtons of Leeds launch the board game Cluedo?
items.reveal: Answer: 1949. Dreamed up in wartime Britain to pass the hours indoors.

items.prompt: When was the very first FA Cup final played?
items.reveal: Answer: 1872. Wanderers lifted it, at the Kennington Oval.

items.prompt: When did Dr. No, the very first James Bond film, reach cinemas?
items.reveal: Answer: 1962. Sean Connery, a Walther PPK, and sixty-odd years of sequels.

items.prompt: When did Channel 4 launch, opening with Countdown?
items.reveal: Answer: 1982. A new channel, and a clock that's been ticking ever since.

items.prompt: When was the famous surgeon's photograph of the Loch Ness Monster published?
items.reveal: Answer: 1934. Much later, it was confessed to be a hoax.

items.prompt: When was Dolly the Sheep, the first cloned mammal, born?
items.reveal: Answer: 1996. Named after Dolly Parton, for reasons best not dwelt upon.

items.prompt: When did Arsenal go through an entire league season unbeaten?
items.reveal: Answer: 2004. Thirty-eight games, not a single defeat.

items.prompt: When did Frankie Dettori ride all seven winners on a single card at Ascot?
items.reveal: Answer: 1996. The bookies wept.

items.prompt: When were the world's first traffic lights installed outside Parliament?
items.reveal: Answer: 1868. Gas-powered, and they promptly exploded.

items.prompt: When did Stephen Hawking publish A Brief History of Time?
items.reveal: Answer: 1988. The best-selling book that almost nobody actually finished.

items.prompt: When did a British-invented CT scanner scan its first patient?
items.reveal: Answer: 1971. Funded, improbably, by profits from the Beatles' record label.

items.prompt: When was Bagpuss first shown on children's television?
items.reveal: Answer: 1974. Only thirteen episodes were ever made.

items.prompt: When was the first London Marathon run?
items.reveal: Answer: 1981. The two leaders crossed the line holding hands. Very British.

items.prompt: When did John Logie Baird demonstrate the first working television?
items.reveal: Answer: 1926. A ventriloquist's dummy, flickering, in a Soho attic.

items.prompt: When did the London Eye open to the public?
items.reveal: Answer: 2000. Meant to be temporary.

items.prompt: When was Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone first published?
items.reveal: Answer: 1997. A first print run of just 500 copies.

items.prompt: When did Dennis Taylor beat Steve Davis on the final black?
items.reveal: Answer: 1985. 18.5 million watched him wag his finger, past midnight.

items.prompt: When did Helen Sharman become the first Briton in space?
items.reveal: Answer: 1991. A chemist from Sheffield who answered an advert on the radio.
